title: dedicated-autoscaler-priority-burst-util-reporting-enhancement-v2
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: Improve dedicated fleet autoscaler stability and observability for priority routing and burst behavior. Customers on Dedicated reported unpredictable burst throttling during sudden spike patterns which caused tail latency regressions and poor utilization signals. This change introduces (1) a token-bucket smoothing layer for priority lanes, (2) clearer throughput-guarantee accounting for reserved pools, and (3) expanded utilization and burst reporting exports to the telemetry pipeline so operations can correlate throttling events with queue/backlog metrics. Changes are backwards-compatible runtime-side; configuration flags gate the new smoothing behavior and telemetry schema provides compatibility keys. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked (ENG-1824) - [x] unit & integration tests - [x] load tests in perf-canary - [x] telemetry schema migration plan - [x] staged rollout and kill-switch in place Rollout: feature gated by runtime config flag "priority_burst_smoothing_v2" (off by default). Rollout plan: enable for internal test fleet, then 10% of customer fleets for 48h, monitor regression alerts, increase to 100% if stable. Observability: new metrics added: dedicated_priority_token_fill, dedicated_priority_drain_rate, dedicated_pool_throughput_guarantee_hit, dedicated_pool_burst_throttle_count. Telemetry export includes event tags: "priority_lane", "burst_smoothing_applied", and original request token metadata. Backwards compatibility: default behavior unchanged until flag enabled. No config file format changes required for existing customers. Migration: telemetry backends will receive new metric names; downstream dashboards are provided as part of the PR. Impact: expected to reduce transient throttle spikes and smooth tail latency at the cost of a controlled short-term throughput smoothing window. See release_notes for customer-facing summary.
